clue.text: Conductor's coat tails initially clung on to by artful fellow

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the first pieces are held fast by what follows, so they sit directly in front of it

parts.note: an animal's coat is its fur

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the word tails is used

parts.note: a wangler is someone who gets things by artful scheming

explanation.surface: A sly character grips the tails of a conductor's tailcoat.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilhelm Furtwängler was a celebrated German conductor; the surface makes 'coat tails' the tailcoat, but 'coat' and 'tails' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilhelm Furtwängler was a famous German orchestral conductor, chiefly of the Berlin Philharmonic.

clue.text: Following surgery, he enjoys the finest dressing

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
an op is a surgical operation

explanation.surface: After an operation, a patient luxuriates in the best bandages.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy is a man devoted to fine clothes, so he enjoys the finest dressing.

clue.text: No sailor's brought up in desert

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a tar is a sailor; the 's is a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: A man who never went to sea grew up in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses NO + TAR as a whole in this down entry, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat on someone is to betray or abandon them, a colloquial synonym for desert.

clue.text: Appealing to gain a few victories

definitions.meaning: charming and attractive in a sweet way
read as two words, to triumph on some occasions, as in 'you ..., you lose some'

explanation.definitionFit: Winsome describes someone with an appealing, innocent charm, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Pole running into ground: almost an accident

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for the North Pole
earthing is an electrical connection running a current into the ground

explanation.surface: A pole driven into the ground nearly causes a mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is a narrow escape, an occasion when disaster almost happened.

clue.text: Nothing's found in smaller deposit

indicators.note: found in means the zero is placed inside the word for smaller

parts.note: less means smaller in amount
nothing is zero, the letter O; the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: Nothing turns up in a lesser deposit.
explanation.definitionFit: Loess is a fine wind-blown silt laid down as a sedimentary deposit.

clue.text: Weird conjuror joined search

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or weird
a mage is a magician or conjuror

explanation.surface: A strange magician signed up for a hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joined' just links the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To rummage is to search untidily through a collection of things.

clue.text: Note that's very hard

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A musical note described as extremely difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Soh is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale, so it is a musical note.

clue.text: Spinster may feel warmer with this

definitions.text: Spinster may feel warmer with this

parts.words: Spinster may feel warmer with this
parts.note: an unmarried woman is a single person; split differently, the word describes wearing a vest, which would keep anyone warmer

explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is an unmarried person; split after the sixth letter it describes a vest being worn.

clue.text: Horsewhip, or madly adore?

indicators.note: madly signals the letters of the two words being thrown into wild disorder

explanation.surface: A question of whether to beat someone with a whip or idolise them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' rearranges the eleven letters of HORSEWHIP and OR.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship someone as a hero is to adore and idolise them.

clue.text: Ruler gets a poet drunk imbibing wine

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the wine goes inside the jumbled letters
drunk signals the letters of a poet reeling into a new order

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A monarch plies a poet with drink until he is drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles A POET into POATE; 'imbibing' then wraps those letters round the wine, a Spanish red solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: A potentate is a monarch or ruler with great power.

clue.text: Police district to staff with soldiers

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it
OR means other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Bringing troops in to staff a police area.
explanation.walkthrough: MANOR is British police slang for the area a station covers.
explanation.definitionFit: In British police slang a manor is the district a particular force or officer patrols.

clue.text: Worker dismissed may need it

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
out means dismissed, as a batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone who has been sacked might need state help.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a worker who is out may need charity.
explanation.definitionFit: A handout is a gift of money or food to the needy, which a sacked worker may require.

clue.text: Funny name for ship?

parts.note: an amusing name for a vessel, also hinting at a comic operetta named after a fictional Royal Navy ship called after a child's apron

explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's comic operetta is named after a ship called after a child's apron, a funny vessel name.

clue.text: Animal circumventing barrier — gulp!

indicators.note: circumventing means going round, so the animal's letters surround the barrier

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
a wall is a barrier

explanation.surface: A creature getting round a fence gives a gasp.
explanation.definitionFit: To gulp food or drink is to swallow it quickly.

clue.text: Gold's unmoveable when river infiltrates seriously

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold; the 's is a link

indicators.note: infiltrates means the river's letter gets inside the word for unmoveable

parts.note: steely means hard and unyielding, unmoveable
R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: Gold stays put while a river seeps into it, gravely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infiltrates' sets the river letter inside the word for unmoveable, making STERELY; 'Gold's' contributes only the symbol, its 's acting as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Austerely means in a stern, serious manner, without frivolity.

clue.text: Script one revised for examiner

indicators.note: revised means altered, so the letters of script one are rewritten in a new order

explanation.surface: An examiner corrects a draft of a script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges the nine letters of SCRIPT ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is an official who examines things, such as schools or tickets.

clue.text: Scornful despot executed those taking part in charge

indicators.note: executed means beheaded, so the despot loses his first letter

parts.note: a tsar was an autocratic Russian ruler
the cast are those taking part in a play

explanation.surface: A tyrant put to death contemptuously those involved in the indictment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' beheads TSAR, removing T to leave SAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcastic means scornful and mocking in a cutting way.

clue.text: Getting in cross at last, forward's delivery curling through air

parts.note: in means getting in, as in elected or arrived

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word cross

parts.note: a winger is a forward playing on the wing; the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: A winger gets a cross in at last and it curls through the air.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an inswinger is a ball that swerves in towards the batsman; the football surface misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: An inswinger is a cricket delivery that swings in the air towards the batsman.

clue.text: I tear in, disturbed by lack of action

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters of I tear in are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tears into another, upset by their idleness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges the seven letters of I TEAR IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a tendency to do nothing, a lack of action or movement.

clue.text: Nip in and steal a little

definitions.meaning: to squeeze sharply between finger and thumb
a small amount, as of salt held between fingers

explanation.definitionFit: Pinch means to nip, slang for steal, and a small amount such as a pinch of salt.

clue.text: Choose to cut staff — it's needed to break new ground

definitions.text: it's needed to break new ground

parts.note: to pick is to choose
to axe is to cut jobs or staff

explanation.surface: Choosing to lay off workers is needed for a fresh start.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickaxe is a digging tool used to break up hard ground.

clue.text: Staying young: ladies would like to

definitions.text: Staying young: ladies would like to

parts.words: Staying young: ladies would like to
parts.note: never growing old; read as two words, it is what many women wish they would do over the years

explanation.definitionFit: Ageless means never growing old; split in two it describes ageing less, which many wish for.

clue.text: Son left to exercise

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A son has gone off to work out.
explanation.definitionFit: Sport is physical exercise or athletic activity.

clue.text: Gunners return to fix light

indicators.note: return means turn back, so the gunners' letters are read backwards

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
to clamp is to fix firmly in place

explanation.surface: Artillerymen come back to repair a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses the Gunners' abbreviation; the Royal Artillery are traditionally called the Gunners in the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc lamp is an electric light producing its glow from an arc between electrodes.

clue.text: Beast almost exhibits female personality

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for beast is dropped

parts.note: an animal is a beast

explanation.surface: A creature nearly shows a womanly character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' removes the final L of ANIMAL; 'exhibits' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jungian psychology the anima is the feminine side of a man's personality.

clue.text: Public assembling round green

parts.note: O is round in shape
vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: People gathering on a village green in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembling' just links the pieces; VERT is the heraldic word for green.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, in public view, not hidden.

clue.text: Drive out vehicles reversing into French river

indicators.note: into means the vehicles go inside the name of the river

parts.note: the Oise is a river in northern France

indicators.note: reversing means the word for vehicles is read backwards

parts.note: carts are horse-drawn vehicles

explanation.surface: Drivers back their cars into a river in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns the vehicles round to STRAC, and 'into' places that run within the French river.
explanation.definitionFit: To ostracise someone is to exclude or drive them out of a group.

clue.text: Keep watch on centre of storm

definitions.meaning: the calm middle of a hurricane

explanation.definitionFit: To eye is to watch closely, and the calm centre of a hurricane is its eye.

clue.text: City bank hasn't opened

indicators.note: hasn't opened means the word lacks its first letter

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on

explanation.surface: A city bank has not opened for business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't opened' drops the R of RELY; Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.

clue.text: Diplomatic incident? This is where documents may lie

definitions.meaning: playfully, a legal case involving an embassy official

definitions.text: This is where documents may lie

explanation.definitionFit: An attaché case is a slim briefcase; whimsically it is also a case concerning a diplomatic attaché.
